intro: I’m Evie (Yuxin) Hou, a sociology researcher working across social research and AI.
approach: I like learning unfamiliar things, trying ideas quickly, and following a good question across disciplines.
role: Third-year Sociology PhD student at Peking University · Visiting Student Research Collaborator at Princeton for one year.

projects.name: SSDataAgent
projects.summary: How should an agent simulate a survey population—and what does a good benchmark score actually tell us?
projects.note: Empirical-copula transfer, information-access constraints, and the difference between statistical fidelity and record copying.

projects.name: Mind Imprint
projects.summary: How can AI offer students structured thinking tools while leaving them responsible for the thinking?
projects.note: Schema-defined cards, recorded learning actions, and a concrete fix for completing project-level cards without a source document.

projects.name: AI attitudes across social media
projects.summary: How can social-media labeling stay inspectable when model responses fail and long runs need to resume?
projects.note: Explicit label validation, provider provenance, and partitioned Parquet outputs for resumable Weibo/Twitter processing.

education: My path began in mechanical engineering and education at Tsinghua, before I joined Peking University’s Center for Social Research in September 2024.
